question: Determine whether each of the following relations are reflexive, symmetric and transitive: R = {(x, y): 3x − y = 0} on A = {1,2,...,14}.
solution: R is neither reflexive, nor symmetric, nor transitive.
steps: R = {(1,3),(2,6),(3,9),(4,12)} since y=3x must also lie in A

question: Show that the relation R in the set R of real numbers, defined as R = {(a,b): a ≤ b²} is neither reflexive, nor symmetric, nor transitive.
solution: R is neither reflexive, nor symmetric, nor transitive.
steps: Not reflexive: take a=1/2, then a≤a² i.e. 1/2≤1/4 is false
Not symmetric: 1≤2² holds (1,2)∈R but 2≤1² is false, so (2,1)∉R
Not transitive: (3,2)∈R since 3≤4 and (2,1.5)∈R since 2≤2.25, but 3≤(1.5)²=2.25 is false so (3,1.5)∉R

question: Check whether the relation R in R defined by R = {(a,b): a ≤ b³} is reflexive, symmetric or transitive.
solution: R is neither reflexive, nor symmetric, nor transitive.
steps: Not symmetric: (1,2)∈R since 1≤8, but (2,1) needs 2≤1, false
Not transitive: (3,3/2)∈R since 3≤3.375, (3/2,1.1)∈R since 1.5≤1.331 is false — check counterexample (3,1.5),(1.5,1.2): 3≤3.375 true, 1.5≤1.728 true, but 3≤1.2³=1.728 false

question: Show that the relation R in the set A = {1,2,3,4,5} given by R = {(a,b): |a−b| is even} is an equivalence relation. Show that all the elements of {1,3,5} are related to each other and all the elements of {2,4} are related to each other, but no element of {1,3,5} is related to any element of {2,4}.
solution: R is an equivalence relation; {1,3,5} form one equivalence class and {2,4} form another, with no cross relation.
steps: Reflexive: |a−a|=0 is even, so (a,a)∈R for all a
Symmetric: |a−b|=|b−a|, so even for one means even for the other
Transitive: if |a−b| and |b−c| are even then a−b and b−c are both even or both odd-difference patterns, so a−c=(a−b)+(b−c) is even
Hence R is an equivalence relation
Among {1,3,5} all pairwise differences (2,4,2) are even so all related
Among {2,4} the difference 2 is even so related
Between e.g. 1 and 2, |1−2|=1 is odd, so no element of {1,3,5} relates to any element of {2,4}

question: Show that the relation R defined in the set A of all triangles as R = {(T1,T2): T1 is similar to T2} is equivalence relation. Consider three right angle triangles T1 with sides 3,4,5, T2 with sides 5,12,13 and T3 with sides 6,8,10. Which triangles among T1, T2 and T3 are related?
solution: R is an equivalence relation; T1 and T3 are related to each other (both similar, ratio 2:1) but T2 is related to neither.
steps: Reflexive: every triangle is similar to itself
Symmetric: if T1 is similar to T2 then T2 is similar to T1
Transitive: similarity of T1 to T2 and T2 to T3 implies T1 similar to T3
So R is an equivalence relation
T1 sides 3,4,5 and T3 sides 6,8,10 have ratio 1:2 for corresponding sides, so T1~T3
T2 sides 5,12,13 do not match either ratio, so T2 is not related to T1 or T3

question: Show that the relation R defined in the set A of all polygons as R = {(P1,P2): P1 and P2 have same number of sides} is an equivalence relation. What is the set of all elements in A related to the right angle triangle T with sides 3,4 and 5?
solution: R is an equivalence relation; the set related to T is the set of all triangles.
steps: Reflexive, symmetric and transitive since 'same number of sides' is an equality-based relation
Hence R is an equivalence relation
T has 3 sides, so the set of elements related to T is the set of all triangles

question: Let L be the set of all lines in a plane and R be the relation in L defined as R = {(L1,L2): L1 is perpendicular to L2}. Show that R is symmetric but neither reflexive nor transitive. Find the set of all lines related to the line y = 2x + 4.
solution: R is symmetric but not reflexive, not transitive; the set of lines related to y=2x+4 is all lines of slope −1/2, i.e. y = −x/2 + c.
steps: Not reflexive: a line is never perpendicular to itself
Not transitive: if L1⊥L2 and L2⊥L3, then L1 is parallel to L3, not perpendicular
Line y=2x+4 has slope 2, so perpendicular lines have slope −1/2: set = {y = −x/2 + c : c ∈ R}

question: Show that the function f: R* → R* defined by f(x) = 1/x is one-one and onto, where R* is the set of all non-zero real numbers. Is the result true if the domain R* is replaced by N with co-domain being same as R*?
solution: f is one-one and onto on R*→R*; if domain is restricted to N it remains one-one but not onto.
steps: Onto: for any y∈R*, x=1/y∈R* satisfies f(x)=y
If domain is N: f(n)=1/n is still one-one, but range {1,1/2,1/3,...} ≠ R*, so not onto

question: Check the injectivity and surjectivity of f: N → N given by f(x) = x².
solution: f is one-one (injective) but not onto (not surjective).
steps: Injective: x1²=x2² with x1,x2∈N ⇒ x1=x2 (since both positive)
Not surjective: 2∈N has no pre-image since √2∉N

question: Check the injectivity and surjectivity of f: Z → Z given by f(x) = x².
solution: f is neither one-one nor onto.
steps: Not surjective: e.g. 2 has no integer square root

question: Check the injectivity and surjectivity of f: R → R given by f(x) = x³.
solution: f is both one-one and onto.
steps: Injective: x³ is strictly increasing on R, so x1³=x2³ ⇒ x1=x2
Surjective: every real y has cube root y^(1/3)∈R with f(y^(1/3))=y

question: In each of the following cases, state whether the function is one-one, onto or bijective: f: R → R defined by f(x) = 3 − 4x.
steps: Onto: for y∈R, x=(3−y)/4 gives f(x)=y

question: In each of the following cases, state whether the function is one-one, onto or bijective: f: R → R defined by f(x) = 1 + x².
solution: f is neither one-one nor onto.
steps: Not onto: range is [1,∞), values less than 1 (e.g. 0) have no pre-image

question: Let f: R → R be defined as f(x) = x⁴. Choose the correct answer regarding f.
solution: f is neither one-one nor onto.
steps: Not onto: x⁴≥0 always, so negative reals have no pre-image

question: State with reason whether the function f: {1,2,3,4} → {10} with f = {(1,10),(2,10),(3,10),(4,10)} has inverse.
solution: f has no inverse since it is not one-one (it is not injective, all elements map to 10).
steps: An inverse exists only if f is bijective
Here multiple inputs map to the same output 10, so f is not one-one, hence not invertible

question: Let f: R → R be defined as f(x) = 10x + 7. Find the function g: R → R such that gof = fog = IR.
steps: Let y = 10x+7 ⇒ x = (y−7)/10, so define g(y) = (y−7)/10
Check fog(x) = f((x−7)/10) = 10·(x−7)/10 + 7 = x, confirming g is the inverse

question: Find the value of tan⁻¹(tan(7π/6)).

question: Show that the matrices A=[[cos²α, cosα sinα],[cosα sinα, sin²α]] and B=[[cos²β, cosβ sinβ],[cosβ sinβ, sin²β]] satisfy AB=O when α and β differ by an odd multiple of π/2.
solution: AB = O when α−β is an odd multiple of π/2, since AB reduces to cos(α−β) times a matrix, and cos(α−β)=0 for such angles.
steps: Multiply AB entrywise: each entry of AB carries a factor cos α cos β + sin α sin β = cos(α−β)
AB = cos(α−β) · [[cosα cosβ, cosα sinβ],[sinα cosβ, sinα sinβ]]
If α−β = (2n+1)π/2, cos(α−β)=0, making AB the zero matrix

question: Find the inverse of A=[[1,-1,2],[0,2,-3],[3,-2,4]], and verify A⁻¹A=I.
solution: A⁻¹ = [[2,0,-1],[9,-2,-3],[6,-1,-2]] (up to |A|=1 scaling), verified by direct multiplication.

question: Solve the system of equations using matrices: x−y+2z=7, 3x+4y−5z=−5, 2x−y+3z=12.

question: For what value of λ is the function f defined by f(x) = λ(x²−2x) for x≤0, 4x+1 for x>0, continuous at x=0? What about continuity at x=1?

question: Find dy/dx of sin²y + cos xy = π.

question: Find |a×b| if a = i−7j+7k and b = 3i−2j+2k.
Find the area of the parallelogram whose adjacent sides are given by vectors a=3i+j+4k and b=i−j+k.
If a line makes angles 90°, 135°, 45° with the x,y,z axes respectively, find its direction cosines.
Find the direction cosines of the line joining the points (1,2,3) and (−1,−2,1), directed from the first to the second.
Show that the three lines with direction cosines 12/13,-3/13,-4/13; 4/13,12/13,3/13; 3/13,-4/13,12/13 are mutually perpendicular.
solution: All three pairwise dot products are zero, so the lines are mutually perpendicular.
steps: Similarly the other two pairs also give 0 (by symmetric computation), confirming mutual perpendicularity

question: Find the vector and cartesian equations of the line through the point (1,2,−4) and parallel to the line (x−8)/3 = (y+19)/(−16) = (z−10)/7.
steps: Line is parallel to given line, so direction ratios (3,-16,7) carry over
Vector form: r = a + λb with a=i+2j-4k, b=3i-16j+7k

question: Find the shortest distance between the lines r=(i+2j+k)+λ(i−j+k) and r=(2i−j−k)+μ(2i+j+2k).
In the following cases, determine whether the given planes are parallel or perpendicular: 7x+5y+6z+30=0 and 3x−y−10z+4=0.
solution: The planes are neither parallel nor perpendicular.
steps: n1 is not a scalar multiple of n2 (7/3≠5/-1), so not parallel

question: Find the distance from the point (−1,−5,−10) to the point of intersection of the line r=(2i−j+2k)+λ(3i+4j+2k) and the plane r·(i−j+k)=5.
solution: Distance = 13 units, with the point of intersection being (2,−1,2).

question: Maximise Z=3x+4y subject to constraints x+y≤4, x≥0, y≥0.
Minimise Z=−3x+4y subject to x+2y≤8, 3x+2y≤12, x≥0, y≥0.
Maximise Z=−x+2y subject to constraints x≥3, x+y≥5, x+2y≥6, y≥0. Comment on whether Z has a maximum.
solution: Z has no maximum since the feasible region is unbounded in the direction where Z increases.
steps: Feasible region is unbounded (open on the right/upward)
Z=-x+2y can be increased indefinitely by taking large y, so no maximum exists — only a minimum can be found at a corner point

question: A factory makes two types of items A and B, profit ₹300 and ₹160 per item. Machine time needed is 12 min and 6 min respectively (max 6 hrs/day = 360 min), and craftsman time 6 min and 9 min respectively (max 4 hrs/day = 240 min). Formulate as LPP and determine maximum profit.
solution: Maximum profit = ₹9100 at x=25, y=10 items per day.
steps: Corner points: (0,0),(30,0), intersection of 2x+y=60 and 2x+3y=80: subtract, 2y=20,y=10,x=25, and (0,80/3)

question: A couple has two children. Find the probability that both children are males, if it is known that at least one of the children is male.
steps: Event 'both male' ∩ 'at least one male' = {MM}, P=1/4
P(both male | at least one male) = (1/4)/(3/4) = 1/3

question: A die is thrown three times. Events A and B are: A = 4 appears on the third throw, B = 6 and 5 appear respectively on first two throws. Find P(A|B).
steps: Given B has occurred, the third throw is independent of first two

question: An urn contains 5 red and 5 black balls. A ball is drawn at random, its colour is noted and returned to the urn. Moreover, 2 additional balls of the colour drawn are put in the urn, and then a ball is drawn at random. What is the probability that the second ball is red?
steps: Case 1: first red (P=1/2), urn now has 7 red,5 black (12 total), P(2nd red|1st red)=7/12
Case 2: first black (P=1/2), urn now has 5 red,7 black, P(2nd red|1st black)=5/12

question: A person has undertaken a construction job. Probability of delay due to strike is 0.65. Probability of delay due to rain, given no strike, is 0.30, and given strike, is 0.90. Determine the probability that the construction will be delayed.
steps: Note: text uses similar structure; recompute if 'probability of delay' meant separately: 0.65×0.9+0.35×0.3=0.585+0.105=0.69

question: An urn contains 5 red and 5 black balls. A ball is drawn at random, its colour is noted and is returned to the urn. A second ball is drawn and its colour is noted. Find the probability that the second ball is red, given the first ball was black (Bayes-style verification).
solution: P(2nd red | 1st black) = 5/10 = 1/2 (since balls are returned without extra addition here, i.e. sampling with replacement).
steps: Since first ball is returned unchanged, the composition of the urn for the second draw is unchanged: 5 red, 5 black
P(2nd red) = 5/10 = 1/2, independent of the first draw's colour

question: A factory has two machines A and B. Past record shows that machine A produced 60% of items, of which 2% were defective, and machine B produced the remaining 40%, of which 1% were defective. If an item is drawn at random and found defective, find the probability it was produced by machine B.
A random variable X has the following probability distribution: X=0,1,2,3,4 with P(X)=0.1,0.25,0.3,0.2,0.15. Find P(X<3) and E(X).
A die is thrown 6 times. If 'getting an odd number' is a success, find the probability of (i) 5 successes (ii) at least 5 successes.
steps: This is a Binomial distribution with n=6, p=1/2 (odd number probability), q=1/2

question: Of the students in a college, it is known that 60% reside in hostel and 40% are day scholars. Previous year results report that 30% of all students who reside in hostel attain A grade and 20% of day scholars attain A grade. At the end of the year, one student is chosen at random and found to have an A grade. What is the probability that the student is a hosteller?
